cases.name: two-commits
cases.desc: Two records, each ETB-committed

cases.name: torn-tail
cases.desc: Uncommitted trailing record is skipped

cases.name: batch-block
cases.desc: Two records under one commit form one atomic block

cases.name: escaped-etb-in-text-not-commit
cases.desc: DLE ETB inside text is data; nothing is committed

cases.name: etb-in-text-cuts
cases.desc: A raw ETB inside open text is a commit: the block is damaged, and later commits are found

cases.name: etb-in-level-cuts
cases.desc: A raw ETB inside an open level is a commit: that block is damaged

cases.name: malformed-block-damaged
cases.desc: Any error inside a committed block damages that block alone; its bounds come from the ETB

cases.name: late-header-row-damaged
cases.desc: A header row after records is an error, so its block is damaged

cases.name: batch-block-damaged
cases.desc: A batch with one bad record is one damaged block: its sound records are not delivered

cases.name: payload-then-text-damaged
cases.desc: What follows a payload begins the next block; text with no record there is an error, so that block is damaged

cases.name: heading-committed
cases.desc: The SYN heading is committed with the first ETB like anything else

cases.name: header-row-committed
cases.desc: A header row is committed like a record

cases.name: payload-in-committed-region
cases.desc: ETB payload extends committed_end but is excluded from the block

cases.name: torn-open-text
cases.desc: A tail that leaves text open is torn

cases.name: torn-lone-dle
cases.desc: A tail ending in a lone DLE is torn

cases.name: em-tail-not-torn
cases.desc: EM after the last commit opens the raw region, which is not data of the log: not torn

cases.name: tail-only-layout
cases.desc: A tail of layout alone is not torn

cases.name: tail-eot
cases.desc: EOT after the last commit closes the log and is not torn

cases.name: tail-comment
cases.desc: A comment after the last commit is not torn

cases.name: empty-stream
cases.desc: Empty buffer: no commits, not torn
